Subjugate

/SUB-juh-gayt/ - the stress falls on SUB · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Subjugate means to conquer a people and bring them under complete control.

Rather than subjugate the forest tribes outright, the new governor tried treaties first — and was recalled within a year for 'weakness.'

Worked Example

No army subjugated the copper valley; the consortium did it with ledgers — company houses, company stores, company courts — until no family could quit, vote, or leave.

Conquer and defeat name the battle; subjugate names the aftermath. Victory is where subjugation starts — the word means a people bent under lasting control, paying, obeying, and answering to the victor long after the fighting ends.

How Subjugate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

conquer

conquer: to defeat and take — the battle, where subjugation is the long aftermath

oppress

oppress: to weigh cruelly on a people — no conquest required

Antonyms

liberate

liberate: to set a people free from control

emancipate

emancipate: to release formally from bondage or restriction

How Strong Is It? — defeat → conquer → subjugate → enslave

defeat vs. subjugate

defeat vs. subjugate: Defeating a people is far milder than subjugating them — the battle is lost, but their laws, lands, and lives may go on unchanged.

conquer vs. subjugate

conquer vs. subjugate: Conquering stops short of subjugating — the victor takes the territory, while subjugation bends the people themselves under lasting control.

enslave vs. subjugate

enslave vs. subjugate: Enslaving goes even further than subjugating — beyond control to outright ownership of human beings.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of subjugate.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — sub-

Prefix — sub-: under

Root — jug

Root — jug: yoke — the bar that ties two oxen together (Latin jugum)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: to make, to act (verb-forming)

Put it together

Put it together: Sub- (under) + jug (yoke) + -ate = to bring under the yoke. Rome made the picture literal: a defeated army was marched, stooping, beneath a yoke of spears. To subjugate a people is to fit that harness permanently — you may remember the word yoke itself from earlier in this course.

Use the root in a new word: conjugate

Use the root in a new word: conjugate: In language class we conjugate each new verb, yoking all its forms together into one matched set.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / historical

Subjugate is a heavyweight word for what happens to peoples, not things — histories and human-rights reports are its home. Use 'conquer' for the military event and 'oppress' for cruelty without conquest. Its unit-mate annex takes the land; subjugate takes the people on it; and colonialism names the whole system the two moves build.
